issues.description: Loop invariant for read_from_fifo_when_ready is not stated and the new control flow has an unreachable branch.
issues.detail: After switching to blocking mode the code does `break` out of the outer loop, so the `else: pass` and the new `except BlockingIOError: pass` are only reachable before any data arrives. The invariant ought to be stated: 'before first byte, fd is O_NONBLOCK and we poll; after first byte, fd is blocking and we read to EOF.' Without that comment the next reader cannot tell which branches are live.

issues.description: Blocking read after first byte removes the subprocess-hang escape hatch; termination is no longer obvious.
issues.detail: The previous design used `check_process_exited` plus poll timeout so a stuck writer could not wedge the parent forever. Once we flip to blocking mode the inner `while True: os.read(...)` has no timeout and no process-liveness check. Termination now depends solely on the writer eventually closing the FIFO. State this assumption explicitly, or interleave poll() so a crashed-after-first-byte subprocess does not hang the reader.

issues.description: POSIX guarantee cited in the comment is correct but under-qualified.
issues.detail: Blocking read on a FIFO returns 0 only when *all* write ends are closed and the pipe is empty. If any other process inherited the write fd (e.g., a grandchild from the subprocess), EOF will not arrive and the inner loop blocks indefinitely. A literate comment should name this precondition: 'exactly one writer, and it will close.' Otherwise the proof of termination is incomplete.

issues.description: fcntl mode flip is not restored and is not guarded against failure.
issues.detail: F_SETFL can fail (EBADF, EINVAL on some platforms) and the result is unchecked. More importantly, the fd's flag state is mutated as a side effect with no restoration in a finally block. If a later refactor moves this fd out of the function, the next user will be surprised that O_NONBLOCK is off. Wrap the flip in try/finally or document the ownership invariant.

issues.description: Dead code after the inner break should be deleted, not left as `pass`.
issues.detail: The `else: pass` and `except BlockingIOError: pass` branches now serve only the pre-first-byte phase. Leaving them as bare `pass` with no comment forces the reader to re-derive that fact. Either delete them and let the outer `while not has_blocking_error` continue, or annotate them as 'pre-first-byte only.' Readability is the constraint here.

issues.description: Removal of `has_blocking_error` leaves a now-dead loop guard.
issues.detail: The outer loop condition `while not has_blocking_error` is no longer ever set to True in the new code path; the variable's only assignment was deleted. Either remove the flag entirely and use `while True`, or restore its meaning. A loop guard that cannot change is a small but real readability bug.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The hybrid non-blocking-then-blocking strategy is a reasonable algorithmic choice and the POSIX argument is essentially right, but the invariant ('before first byte: polled non-blocking; after first byte: blocking read to EOF') is nowhere stated, so a future reader cannot tell which of the remaining branches are still live. Termination of the new inner loop rests on assumptions — single writer, writer will close, no inherited write fds — that should be written into the code, not the PR description. The fcntl flip is also unguarded and unrestored. I would land this only after the invariant, the termination argument, and the dead-or-pre-first-byte branches are made explicit in the source.
